title: Which of these is 'roots growing into the tree/sky'?
question:
Your own roots-on sheet from 2026-09-05, magnified 4x at two places. I can see two different things and I think I have been fixing the wrong one.

LEFT: a whole plant rendered pale cream instead of brown, with a thin pale strand curling in the air beside it.
RIGHT: a normal brown tree with a thin 1-cell strand hanging straight down out of the canopy into open air, ending in nothing.

Which did you mean -- or is it something else in that sheet?

Measured on a fresh grove at the same settings (6 seeds, 24,000 frames): 387 root cells have open sky above them but ALL sit at ground level, i.e. ordinary surface roots; only 14 root cells are more than 2 cells above their own collar, worst rise 7. Neither number is large, and the rule I shipped moves both within noise -- so I cannot reproduce what you saw, and I would rather ask than keep guessing.
